- adversarial advocacy
- responsible lawyering
- cause lawyering/moral activist

● Defined by the particular role of a lawyer

● Duty
of zealous advocacy for a
client (i.e. client interests take utmost priority)

○ Lawyers are not morally responsible for
means or ends of their work, as long as it is lawful

● Approach may be more justified for criminal
defense lawyers

○ Prosecutors should be fair and only present
well-grounded facts to the court

● Advantage:

○ Encouraged lawyers to pursue clients’
rights against the power of the state

● Disadvantage:

○ Seen as “amoral” because it sees general
moral theory as irrelevant

○ May lead to excess conflict and
adversarialism in the court process

Frowned
upon in Singapore, as the duty to the court prevails over that of the client

● Defined by the particular role of a lawyer

● Duty
as an officer of the court and guardian of the legal system

○ Balances client’s interests with
maintaining justice and integrity of the legal system

○ Focuses on maintaining institutions of law
and justice in their best form

● Advantage:

○ Addresses problem of lawyers helping
clients to manipulate the legal system

● Disadvantage:

○ Danger of not adequately serving client’s
interests

○ Lawyers may end up serving a corrupt
administration

● Defined by general principles of ethics

● Duty
to do good according to general ethics

○ Not confined by idea of justice in a system

○ Lawyers have personal convictions of how to
do justice

○ Use legal practice to change people,
institutions and the law to conform to general ideas of social and political
justice

● Examples:

○ Representing clients with “worthy causes”
or those who suffered from “injustice”

○ Participation in politicised law reform
activities

■ E.g. constitutional challenges, class
action lawsuits

● Advantage:

○ More proactive role in ensuring justice

○ Persuading clients to do the right thing

● Disadvantage:

○ Tendency to place the lawyer’s ideals above
the client’s interests

○ Neglecting the principle that anyone should
be entitled to legal representation

Front: Why no cause lawyering in SG?
Back:
○ Operation Coldstore
established 3 thematic pillars of SG political life

■ State’s capacity to deploy
detention without trial against political opponents

■ State’s capacity to
characterise political opponents as threats

■ State’s capacity to
characterise critique as a form or political opposition endangering the
‘nation’

○ Mass Media heavily regulated

● Defined by general principles of ethics

● Focuses
on preserving relationships and minimising harm

○ Addresses concrete needs of all parties

○ Ensures that only those that can best bear
harm will receive harm

○ Goal-directed (teleological) view of
relationships

● Advantage:

○ Emphasises dialogue between lawyers and
clients

○ Looks for non-adversarial ways to resolve
disputes

● Disadvantage:

○ May ignore justice in certain situations
(e.g. domestic abuse)
○ Highly conservative and may not address social and
political injustice
